intake_statement: Prove existence of a crystalline Gibbs phase at sufficiently low positive temperature for the three-dimensional Coulomb or Riesz gas in the regimes predicted in the review.
intake_source_status: Campaign ledger formulation, not a verbatim theorem statement from Lewin

primary_source.author: Mathieu Lewin
primary_source.title: Coulomb and Riesz gases: The known and the unknown
primary_source.locator: Section VI, PDF pages 58-59 and 65-66 (zero based); printed pages 59-60 and 66-67
evidence: PDF lines 6651-6675: finite-beta phase transition is nonuniqueness; a solid phase is a periodic probability law, with translated and rotated mixtures distinguished
PDF lines 6714-6775: Theorem 46 gives uniqueness at sufficiently small beta*rho^(s/3) for s>3
PDF lines 7322-7345: d=3 short-range FCC/BCC and long-range Coulomb BCC phase diagrams are numerical expectations

quantifier_correction: The intake does not specify one universal exponent, all densities, or a proved lattice choice. A workable s>3 subproblem fixes s and rho>0 and asks for a sufficiently large finite beta*rho^(s/3) with a symmetry-breaking DLR law. Coulomb s=1 requires a separately specified neutralized long-range ensemble.
